findings.citation: Every relief must clear the parts that enter it by `RELIEF_CLEARANCE`. A design review reported that one relief does not; find it and fix how its depth is derived from the parts that actually enter it.
findings.description: The starting p2_hinge_relief() is already max(screw-T040, T063+nut)+RELIEF_CLEARANCE, which is identical to the harness's own 'need' formula and to the oracle stack.py (the oracle leaves it unchanged). The relief checks pass before any change, so the claimed defective relief does not exist and the task's premise is false.

findings.citation: hinge relief is derived from the screw length, not hard-coded
findings.description: The check recomputes need with the exact formula max(screw-T040, T063+HINGE_NUT_H)+RELIEF_CLEARANCE. It rejects other valid derivations, for example one that also counts the nut thickness above the screw tip. It also gives no signal about the claimed bug.

findings.citation: standoff and screw callouts in whole mm
findings.description: No check covers the M1.6x6 screw callout in the BOM. No check enforces that the hand-post length comes from STANDOFF_CATALOG beyond the literal HAND_STANDOFF==5.0. No check covers the README rows other than the crystal and lid rows.

findings.citation: Every relief must clear the parts that enter it by `RELIEF_CLEARANCE`.
findings.description: The relief probes only require depth >= need. A large hard-coded constant passes all three probes, so they do not verify the following required derivation from the parts that actually enter the relief.

findings.citation: Change nothing else: plate, gear-space, carrier, lid and sheet thicknesses and the hand stack heights are fixed by other parts.
findings.description: The preservation check covers several constants but omits T_HAND, GEAR_PITCH_Z, LEVELS behavior, and the individual hand-stack heights documented in ASSEMBLY.md; those fixed values can be changed without failing a clause.

findings.citation: Keep the documents' existing wording and layout otherwise.
findings.description: The document checks extract only selected numbers with regular expressions and do not verify preservation of the remaining wording or layout.

findings.citation: `hardware/stack.py` is the stdlib Z stack-up and hinge model (an excerpt of the CAD design module; `python hardware/stack.py` prints the derived report).
findings.description: The report-consistency clause compares only body_height, closed_height, and crystal_clearance. The report's crystal_underside_above_p2, upper_shell_flange, and p2_hinge_relief values, as well as the script's printed report behavior, can be made inconsistent without detection.
